title: InvenTree Part & Part Category Lifecycle Management and Token Authentication
rawText: Allows authenticated users to manage the complete lifecycle of Part and Part Category entities in InvenTree (>= 0.15.x) through REST API endpoints and web UI interfaces, enforcing hierarchical category tree structures, referential integrity across parts and stock, unique internal part numbers (IPN), multi-facet search/filtering, and token-based authorization (Authorization: Token <token>).

risksIdentified.description: Accidental or unconstrained cascade deletion of a non-empty Part Category causing orphan deletion or unintended detachment of child categories and assigned parts, compromising inventory traceability.
Bypassing token-based authentication on mutating API endpoints (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) allowing unauthenticated or unauthorized callers to alter production part catalogues.
Referential integrity violation when attempting to delete a Part currently referenced in active Stock Items or Bill of Materials (BOM) components, causing data corruption in manufacturing workflows.

Circular parent category hierarchy cycles (e.g., Category A -> Category B -> Category A) resulting in infinite recursion, stack overflows, or broken tree rendering during UI navigation and pathstring recalculation.
Race conditions and lost updates during concurrent PUT or PATCH mutations to /api/part/{id}/ regarding active status, IPN, or category assignments without optimistic concurrency control.

Search and multi-facet filtering query latency degradation exceeding the 2,000ms - 3,000ms SLA on catalogues exceeding 10,000 parts when database indices on category, active flag, and IPN/name are absent.
State desynchronization between Category Tree View expansion state and Part List table pagination/filter facets during rapid client-side navigation.

ambiguities: Cascade vs Block policy on category deletion: FA-005 specifies deletion may cascade or be rejected depending on instance configuration; tests must assert explicit rejection with HTTP 400 when cascade is disabled and require validation of configurable behavior.

Mutating endpoint unauthorized response code: FA-013 states unauthenticated requests must return HTTP 403 Forbidden, while standard Django REST Framework token authentication returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized; both status codes must be handled and validated in security test matrices.

Unauthenticated catalogue read access: FA-002 and FA-008 indicate public read access depends on instance configuration (LOGIN_REQUIRED setting); test suites must verify behavior under both public and private catalogue configurations.

Part search field boundaries: FA-007 specifies search matching name and IPN, while description search is unstated in rule 5; clarification boundaries set search index to name and IPN substring matching.
Form submission debouncing and latency: UI flow FA-012 mentions real-time or submit search updates; UI automated tests should assert a 300ms debounce threshold for live filtering.
